concept.name: Financial market
concept.definition: An organized or decentralized arrangement in which participants exchange financial assets, funds, and risk exposures and thereby establish prices. Financial markets perform two core functions: channeling savings to issuers in the primary market and providing liquidity and price discovery through secondary trading.
concept.intuition: It is where people who have money meet people who need it, and where people holding risk trade it to people willing to bear it; the byproduct of all that trading is a price.
concept.mechanics: Buyers and sellers submit orders to centralized venues (exchanges, ECNs) or negotiate bilaterally through dealers (OTC); executed trades are cleared and settled through market infrastructures, and the stream of transactions aggregates information into quoted prices.
concept.failure_modes: Prices stop reflecting available information when liquidity evaporates, information is severely asymmetric, or trading is manipulated; in crises, markets can gap, halt, or close entirely.
concept.misconceptions: 'The market' is not a single place or entity but a network of competing venues and intermediaries; a quoted price is the outcome of transactions, not an appraisal of intrinsic value.
concept.example: A company raises $500 million by selling new shares to investors in the primary market; those shares then trade among investors on exchanges and alternative trading systems in the secondary market.

citations.source: SEC, Concept Release on Equity Market Structure (Release No. 34-61358)
